name: implement
description: Implement flow: read an approved design artifact, write the implementation-plan checkpoint, then actually implement the feature with a real, passing test.
prompt: Run the installed implement skill protocol for this fixture in verbose mode; do not do an ad-hoc summary. Read `plans/widget-tax-design.md` as the approved design artifact for ticket WID-9. If the current host is Codex, load the installed Codex delegate-context protocol and emit its verbose load stamp, but do not dispatch a subagent because this fixture has one dependent implementation task. Write Phase 1's implementation plan (goal, architecture, files touched, task decomposition) and, per the configured `implementation_plan_created` lifecycle action, write the checkpoint artifact to `checkpoints/implementation_plan_created-WID-9.md` using the standard checkpoint sections (Checkpoint Metadata, State Summary, Key Context, Decisions, Next Step, Open Risks / Questions), then update `.beislid/checkpoints/latest.json` with the implementation_plan_created pointer entry (event, path, ticket, branch, source_skill, written_at) - this pointer file must stay untracked, never committed. Then execute Phase 3 with TDD: modify `export_widgets(items, path, tax_rate=None)` in `src/widget_export.py` so that when `tax_rate` is given, each written CSV row gets an extra `tax_rate` column equal to the given value (header gains a `tax_rate` column too), and existing no-tax-rate behavior is unchanged. Add a real test function to `tests/test_widget_export.py` (e.g. `test_export_widgets_with_tax_rate`) that writes a CSV via `export_widgets` with a tax_rate and asserts the extra column and value are present, and keep the existing test passing. Commit your implementation with a descriptive message. Do not use real network. FINAL RESPONSE REQUIREMENT: state the checkpoint path you wrote and the name of the new test function.
